title: Bring the item a crewmate points at
instruction: The crewmate cannot speak and is pointing at the item they need. Put that item upright on the white tray and leave every other item where it is.
context: People who cannot speak point at what they need: after a stroke, while intubated, or in a loud module with a failed headset. An assistive robot has to follow the line of the forearm, palm and finger to the item meant, then set it on the white hand-off tray a carer serves from, without reaching toward the person. A fixed crew stand-in across the table points 30 degrees outboard of straight toward the arms; only the green cylinder lies on that line. The red one is nearest the fingertip and straight in front of the left arm. The blue one is straight toward the arms from the fingertip, nearest the left arm's base and farthest from the crewmate. The yellow one is nearest the tray. Each of those habits fails, and so does bringing all four. The items differ only in colour and the instruction names none, so the gesture is the only cue. The motor part is one pick and place; the test is grounding the gesture and disturbing nothing else. A 1 g tabletop analogue; no microgravity is claimed.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left). Positions are table coordinates in metres, origin on the base line at the midline; the left arm's base is at (0, 0.305) and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every part is a rigid matte primitive with one friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, the crew stand-in, facing the arms: a torso, a block 120 mm deep (x), 300 mm wide and 180 mm tall, slate blue (sRGB 0.30, 0.35, 0.50), standing on the table centred at (0.6475, 0.000); a head, an upright cylinder 120 mm in diameter and 120 mm tall, brown (sRGB 0.45, 0.30, 0.22), standing centred on the torso. Its right forearm, palm and index finger lie on the table end to end on one straight line, the pointing line, which leaves the fingertip at (0.330, 0.245) in the direction (-0.866, 0.500), 30 degrees outboard of straight toward the arms. Each block's sizes are given along the line, across it, then height: the finger, 80 x 18 x 16 mm, brown, centred at (0.365, 0.225); the palm, 60 x 80 x 30 mm (60 mm along the line, 80 mm across it), brown, centred at (0.425, 0.190); the forearm, 140 x 60 x 45 mm, slate blue (a sleeve), centred at (0.512, 0.140), its back corner touching the torso's front face at x = 0.5875. Fixed, the tray, all white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.95), centred at (0.170, 0.070): a floor 90 x 90 x 6 mm and four rim walls 6 mm thick and 15 mm tall standing on the table around it, so the outer outline is 102 x 102 mm and the floor top is 6 mm above the table. Loose: four identical cylinders 40 mm in diameter and 60 mm tall, 50 g each, standing upright. Green (sRGB 0.20, 0.65, 0.25) at (0.200, 0.320), on the pointing line 150 mm past the fingertip. Red (sRGB 0.85, 0.15, 0.15) at (0.335, 0.305), 60 mm from the fingertip, 65 degrees off the line and straight in front of the left arm's base. Blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.85) at (0.130, 0.245), 200 mm from the fingertip straight toward the arms (along -x), 30 degrees off the line. Yellow (sRGB 0.95, 0.80, 0.10) at (0.200, 0.170), 150 mm from the fingertip and 60 degrees off the line, 29 mm from the rim. Every other item is at least 54 mm from the pointing line, and neighbouring items are at least 100 mm apart centre to centre. The right arm is idle at its ready pose. To build it: a foam or wood block for the torso with a can glued on top for the head; three wood blocks glued end to end for the forearm, palm and finger, painted; the tray from 6 mm board with 6 x 15 mm strip glued around it; tape the torso, the arm blocks and the tray to the table; the items cut from 40 mm hardwood dowel and painted.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm withdraws from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level; tilt is the angle between an item's axis and vertical, either end down. The green item is delivered when it rests on the tray floor: lowest point within 3 mm of the floor top (an item standing on the table is 6 mm below it), tilt 10 degrees or less, centre inside the 90 x 90 mm floor, at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s). Another item is on the tray when, seen from above, any part of it reaches 2 mm or more inside the tray's 102 x 102 mm outer outline, at any height: on the floor, leaning on a rim, stacked on the green item or still held over the tray. Another item is in place when it stands upright (tilt 10 degrees or less) on the table (lowest point within 4 mm of the table top) with its centre within 20 mm of its mark. Score 1.0 if the green item is delivered, no other item is on the tray and the red, blue and yellow items are all in place. Score 0.5 if the green item is delivered and no other item is on the tray, but one or more of the others is out of place: moved more than 20 mm, tipped past 10 degrees, lifted or knocked off the table. Score 0 for every other outcome: the green item off the tray, lying, tilted more than 10 degrees, on a rim, held above the floor or still moving, or any other item on or partly on the tray, whatever else happened. The start state scores 0, and so does bringing the item nearest the fingertip and straight in front of the left arm (red), the item straight toward the arms from the fingertip, nearest the left arm's base and farthest from the crewmate (blue), the item nearest the tray (yellow), or all four. Pushing the green item along the table cannot score: the 15 mm rim stops a sliding item, and one tipped over the rim lies down. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. In simulation every test uses each item's centre and quaternion: the lowest point comes from the cylinder's axis, and the outline seen from above is the hull of 24 points on each end circle. The stand-in and the tray are fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which any stand-in block or the tray moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. The scorer reads object poses, not the gripper: in simulation an item held motionless in a scoring place would count; on real arms the photo after the arm parks decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the four items upright back on their marks; the stand-in and the tray do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the in-place rule is measured from the nominal marks, and with jitter an item would start up to 3 cm off its mark and the green one off the pointing line.
fidelity: Approximate: the crewmate is a fixed block stand-in with one straight finger, no motion and no gaze; a real pointing hand is softer and less straight, and people add gaze and a head turn. The items are rigid painted cylinders standing in for supplies. The finger is 18 mm wide, about 3 px at 320 x 176, but forearm, palm and finger make one 280 mm line, about 50 px long. One shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench.
